answer: An agent economy can price identity: every new key burns a small, irrecoverable deposit into a shared vault, sized by a live oracle rather than a fixed fee. When a swarm mints ten thousand wallets, the oracle sees the spike and the deposit rises until a fleet costs more than the payout it could capture. The deposit is sunk, never refunded, so an attacker pays it per fake identity while an honest agent pays once for a lifetime of work. An ocean is counted by currents, not droplets: only deposits that survive a full epoch count as one voice, and scarcity is what makes an opal precious.
